Project home · Results summary

What earlier work predicts for our expression data

Candidate genes for the LTH RNA-seq (D1, D3 and D10, wound section) · Updated 19 November 2026

Earlier Acropora studies point to one clean test. Early wound genes should respond at both temperatures, matching our finding that heat did not slow healing. If heat stalls radial corallites by blocking the regrowth program, skeleton-building genes should be lower in wounded fragments at 31 °C than at 28 °C on D10.

Our timeline. Healing by D1 (24 h after wounding) at both temperatures · axial polyp and corallite formed by about D8 · radial corallites from about D12 at 28 °C, mostly absent at 31 °C · RNA sampled at D1, D3 and D10.

Three gene sets and what each predicts

These sets were compiled before we saw expression results. Testing whether each is over-represented among temperature × wound genes at D1 and D10 tells us which explanation fits, without limiting the genome-wide analysis.

Gene setPrediction at D1Prediction at D10What it would tell us
Early wound responsec-Fos, c-Jun, JNK/ERK, TIR-1/TLR, NF-κB/TRAF6, lectin and complement genesWound effect at both temperatures (heat changed little in A. aspera at 24 h). c-Jun is the one gene where heat amplified the injury response.A second wave is plausible (c-Fos, ERK2, TRAF6 rose again at day 10 in A. aspera).Matches our healing result: heat did not slow early repair.
Regrowth and skeleton buildingGalaxin 2, Saarp2, mucin, Usomp, carbonic anhydrase 2, calicoblast markers, collagensLittle expected yet.Lower in wounded fragments at 31 °C than at 28 °C if heat blocks the regrowth program.The sharpest test of why radial corallites stalled. Han's timing (day 21, slower species) means D10 may be early.
Heat stress and energyRibosomal and mitochondrial genes, redox genes, HSPsHeat effect in wounded and unwounded fragments alike.Same; if regrowth genes are only low where stress genes are high, the story is general stress.Separates an energy explanation from a specific patterning failure. Do not expect big HSP changes (Bonesso).

The studies these predictions rest on

We checked each against the full paper on 19 November 2026.

StudyDesignKey findings for us
Xu et al. 2023A. millepora, aquaria; transcriptomes at 6 h, 24 h, 48 h and polyp regrowth (3–10 d)Wnt, FGF/sprouty, ADAMTS, galaxin and c-Fos (with the JNK cascade) peak at 6 h. Calcium transport is enriched at the growing colony edge, not during regeneration.
van de Water et al. 2015, Mol EcolA. aspera, in situ; qPCR of about 20 immune genes at 16 h and 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 10 dResponses come in waves (<2, 4 and 10 d). c-Fos up 2.3× at day 4 and 2.1× at day 10; ERK2 up at days 2, 4 and 10; c-Jun unchanged. Lesions nearly regenerated by day 10.
van de Water et al. 2015, HydrobiologiaA. aspera, aquaria; 27–29 °C vs 32–33.5 °C for 8 d, then injury; qPCR of 15 genes at 24 hInjury raised c-Fos and c-Jun; heat raised c-Jun further in injured corals. ATF4/5 and TRAF6 showed temperature × injury interactions. Overall, heat changed the injury response little. Two aquaria per temperature.
Bonesso et al. 2017, PeerJA. aspera, tip removal; 26 °C vs 32 °C for 12 d; sampled every 2 dRegrowth complete by day 12 at 26 °C but under 50% at 32 °C. No HSP70/HSP90 upregulation (both down at day 12). Wound-site GFP fluorescence lower under heat.
Han et al. 2025, Commun BiolA. muricata, tip cut; bulk RNA-seq every 3 d to day 39; single-cell RNA-seq at day 21 onlyRegeneration peaks at days 15–27. Galaxin 2 rises mid-to-late and Ca2 rises over time; one calicoblast cluster up-regulates galaxin 2, Saarp2 and mucin, and Ca2 is up in wounded calicoblasts. Ribosomal and mitochondrial genes drop in wounded gastrodermis.

Cautions

  • Timing differs by species and setting. Xu saw the main wound genes peak at 6 h; van de Water saw waves at days 2–4 and 10. Our D1 sample (24 h) may miss the earliest peak.
  • The regrowth genes come from one single-cell study at day 21 in a slower-regenerating species, inferred from trajectories rather than lineage tracing.
  • GFP-like protein results in both injury studies are protein fluorescence, not transcripts, so they do not directly predict RNA-seq.
  • The only heat × injury expression study measured 15 genes at one time point with two aquaria per temperature.
  • Rows marked “not rechecked” below come from the original compilation and have not been verified against the papers.
